chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'd, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the bones of the elephant, is it permissible to sell them or buy them, from which the combs are made? He said: There is no problem. There used to be for my father a comb, or combs, from them.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy and sell elephant bones for making combs in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility (*halal*) of trading elephant bones, specifically for crafting combs, by citing the practical precedent of the Imam’s father. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that items not inherently impure or prohibited can be validly bought and sold if they serve a legitimate utility, reinforcing the flexibility of commercial law in daily life.
